races.paceDynamic: Son Of Wind is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead with Sovereign Banter, An Laochmor and Rattletheonionbag settling just behind in the early positions. The lack of pace pressure means Son Of Wind can dictate fractions and kick clear turning for home before the hold-up horses get organized. With multiple hold-up horses including Oxford Circus, Winemaker, Jered Maddox and Hot To Foxtrot all needing to come from the back, they'll face a traffic nightmare and rely on the leader faltering. This pace setup clearly favors the prominent racers who can track the soft lead and pounce when Son Of Wind weakens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Son Of Wind gets easy fractions and kicks clear at the furlong pole
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows him to save energy for a sustained drive, while the hold-up brigade get caught flat-footed trying to make up too much ground. His style perfectly suits getting first run on this field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Son Of Wind sets steady fractions but gets collared by a well-positioned stalker
scenarios.body: An Laochmor or Sovereign Banter can sit the perfect trip behind the uncontested leader and time their challenge to perfection. They avoid the traffic issues plaguing the hold-up horses while having enough tactical pace to respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Rallies
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is particularly sedate and allows time for a strong closer to organize
scenarios.body: Oxford Circus or Winemaker could find racing room late and use superior class to reel in tired leaders. However, they need significant help from pace collapse and clear running to overcome their poor draws.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Son Of Wind goes too slowly early and multiple horses converge simultaneously
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole with no clear pace advantage. This chaos scenario could suit any horse finding room, but the superior handicapped horses like Winemaker might prevail.

races.paceDynamic: Real Encounter is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the outset, likely getting an uncontested lead in this small field. With most rivals carrying hold-up styles (Aughlish, Meriden, Allsortz, Atallah), there's minimal early pressure, allowing Real Encounter to control fractions. The tactical setup creates a moderate pace that builds gradually, with the bulk of the field relying on late kicks. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel well and finish, as the lone leader may have plenty left in reserve but could be vulnerable to a well-timed closer with genuine ability.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Real Encounter establishes easy fractions and maintains stamina reserves
scenarios.body: The front-runner controls the race unchallenged and kicks clear when the hold-up horses make their moves. His 196-day break becomes less relevant given the tactical advantage of an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the newcomers show superior class and Real Encounter's long layoff tells
scenarios.body: The pace allows talented debutants or improving types to unleash finishing kicks that overwhelm the leader. Quality emerges as the decisive factor over tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Experience Counts
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz or Aughlish benefit from racecourse familiarity and surface knowledge
scenarios.body: The proven performers use their experience to time runs perfectly while newcomers struggle with race positioning. Course form becomes the edge in a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Real Encounter stops quickly and multiple closers arrive together
scenarios.body: The leader's stamina gives way in the final furlong, creating a bunched finish where any of the hold-up horses could prevail. Raw speed in the final 100 yards decides the outcome.

races.paceDynamic: Private Larry and Straight Back Up are the confirmed front runners, though both carry warnings for fading in the finish. Private Larry showed his keen tendencies when failing to stay 1m2f at Navan, while Straight Back Up has been well held in recent efforts. Royal County Glory racing prominently will likely sit just behind the leaders, with the majority of this field preferring to come from off the pace. The early pace should be honest but not destructive, setting up a finish where horses with tactical speed and finishing kick will have the advantage over pure front runners and one-paced hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not too strong through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The prominent racers and those with early speed who can finish will have perfect positioning as the confirmed leaders fade. Royal County Glory and Ferrari Desert can capitalize on ideal race positioning.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Early Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Private Larry goes too fast early and drags Straight Back Up into a pace duel
scenarios.body: The honest pace becomes destructive, suiting the patient hold-up horses who can unleash late runs. Imperial Fighter and Will Be King benefit from the collapse up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Private Larry settles better than usual and gets an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The gelding operation helps Private Larry's temperament and he gets loose on the lead without pressure. Straight Back Up can also benefit if tracking a slower pace than usual.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too slowly and create a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with little pace, favoring horses with the best turn of foot regardless of position. Queen Leila and Ferrari Desert have shown the most natural speed in recent runs.

races.paceDynamic: Jawhary is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead through the early stages. With 11 hold-up horses behind him, the pace will be steady rather than strong, allowing Jawhary to dictate terms without pressure. The large contingent of closers will bunch up in behind, setting up a sprint finish where stamina and tactical positioning become crucial. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours prominent racers like Jawhary who can avoid the traffic problems that will plague the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Jawhary gets a soft lead and stays the trip
scenarios.body: The front runner controls the tempo throughout and has enough left to resist late challenges. Hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from the crowded pack behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Stayer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and stamina tells
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of staying power over tactical speed in the final furlong. Horses with proven course form and stamina reserves benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates significant interference in the straight
scenarios.body: Several hold-up horses get blocked runs and the race falls to those with clear passages. Positioning and luck become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Jawhary goes too slow and gets swamped late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the furlong pole with fresh closers overwhelming the leader. Raw speed trumps tactical advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Ramair and A Pretty Penny are both confirmed front-runners, but with A Pretty Penny now a non-runner, Ramair becomes the sole recognized pace-setter in this seven-runner field. This leaves Ramair potentially uncontested on the lead through the early stages, which could create a steady honest gallop rather than a searching pace. With most runners preferring to be held up (Cameclose, Keepsgettingbetter, Elm Creek, Musashi, Sea Of Dubka), the lack of early pace pressure should suit horses that can travel prominently and have a turn of foot, rather than pure hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Handy
scenarios.trigger: If Ramair gets an easy lead and the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace leaves the field bunched turning for home, favouring horses that can position closer and have acceleration rather than pure closers. Keepsgettingbetter and Elm Creek can travel handier than their hold-up style suggests and benefit from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ramair Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Ramair gets loose on the lead and the field fails to apply enough pressure
scenarios.body: With no other confirmed pace-setters, Ramair could steal a march and prove hard to peg back over this stamina-sapping trip. His fade-in-finish warning becomes less relevant if he gets his own way in front and the pace stays manageable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Develops Late
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses move together turning for home creating a fast finish
scenarios.body: The tactical nature of the early running gives way to a sprint finish that favours the strongest closer. This setup would particularly suit horses with recent form improvement and good finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the handicapper has underestimated one of the reformed horses with gear changes
scenarios.body: Musashi with first-time visor and gelding operation, or Sea Of Dubka stepping into handicaps, could outrun their poor maiden form. The tactical nature of the race could mask their lack of early pace and set up their late run.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Ramair gets an uncontested lead through the first half-mile as this could set up a tactical race that doesn't suit the hold-up majority
Monitor Musashi in the market as first-time visor and gelding operation for Joseph O'Brien could signal significant improvement from poor maiden form
Keep an eye on how aggressively the jockeys ride turning for home as the pace scenario will determine whether hold-up horses get the strong finish they need
Watch Elm Creek's early positioning as he may be able to race handier than his hold-up classification suggests, especially with cheekpieces retained
Observe if Keepsgettingbetter can repeat her last-time finishing kick as she's the only horse in the field with recent winning form
